```{r}
library(survey)
library(car)

data <- read.csv("data/combined_data.csv")

# Replace near-zero corrupted values (e.g. 5.397e-79) with NA across all numeric columns
numeric_cols <- sapply(data, is.numeric)
data[numeric_cols] <- lapply(data[numeric_cols], function(x) {
  x[abs(x) < 1e-10 & x != 0] <- NA
  return(x)
})

# Recode gender
data$Female <- ifelse(data$RIAGENDR == 2, 1, 0)

# Center variables for interaction
data$Fiber_c <- scale(data$total_fiber, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
data$PAD680_c <- scale(data$PAD680, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
data$Sugar_c <- scale(data$total_sugar, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
data$Protein_c <- scale(data$total_protein, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
data$Calories_c <- scale(data$total_calories, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

# Compute total weekly activity minutes from moderate + vigorous leisure-time PA
# Convert frequency to weekly based on reported unit (D=daily, W=weekly, M=monthly, Y=yearly)
freq_to_weekly <- function(freq, unit) {
  ifelse(is.na(freq) | freq >= 9999, NA,
  ifelse(unit == "b'D'", freq * 7,
  ifelse(unit == "b'W'", freq,
  ifelse(unit == "b'M'", freq / 4.33,
  ifelse(unit == "b'Y'", freq / 52, 0)))))
}

data$mod_weekly_freq <- freq_to_weekly(data$PAD790Q, data$PAD790U)
data$PAD800_clean <- ifelse(data$PAD800 >= 9999, NA, data$PAD800)
data$mod_weekly_min <- data$mod_weekly_freq * data$PAD800_clean

data$vig_weekly_freq <- freq_to_weekly(data$PAD810Q, data$PAD810U)
data$PAD820_clean <- ifelse(data$PAD820 >= 9999, NA, data$PAD820)
data$vig_weekly_min <- data$vig_weekly_freq * data$PAD820_clean

# Blank unit = no activity reported = 0 minutes
data$mod_weekly_min[data$PAD790U %in% c("b''", "")] <- 0
data$vig_weekly_min[data$PAD810U %in% c("b''", "")] <- 0

# Total weekly activity: moderate + 2*vigorous (WHO MET-equivalent convention)
data$total_activity_min <- ifelse(
  !is.na(data$mod_weekly_min) & !is.na(data$vig_weekly_min),
  data$mod_weekly_min + 2 * data$vig_weekly_min, NA)
data$total_activity_min <- ifelse(is.na(data$total_activity_min) & !is.na(data$mod_weekly_min),
  data$mod_weekly_min, data$total_activity_min)
data$total_activity_min <- ifelse(is.na(data$total_activity_min) & !is.na(data$vig_weekly_min),
  2 * data$vig_weekly_min, data$total_activity_min)

data$Activity_c <- scale(data$total_activity_min, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Missing Data Audit
# OLS complete cases: 4,493/6,751 (67%). Multivariate: 2,461/6,751 (36%) due to glucose subsample.
key_vars <- c("BMXBMI", "LBXTC", "BMXWAIST", "LBDGLUSI", "PAD680",
              "total_calories", "total_sugar", "total_fiber", "total_protein",
              "RIDAGEYR", "Female")

cat("=== Non-NA counts per variable ===\n")
for (v in key_vars) {
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %d / %d\n", v, sum(!is.na(data[[v]])), nrow(data)))
}

# Effective sample size for OLS models (complete cases across all OLS predictors + outcomes)
ols_vars <- c("BMXBMI", "LBXTC", "total_calories", "total_sugar", "total_fiber",
              "total_protein", "PAD680", "total_activity_min", "RIDAGEYR", "Female")
cat(sprintf("\nComplete cases for OLS models: %d / %d\n",
            sum(complete.cases(data[ols_vars])), nrow(data)))

# Effective sample size for multivariate models
multi_vars <- c("BMXBMI", "BMXWAIST", "LBDGLUSI", "LBXTC",
                "total_calories", "total_sugar", "total_protein",
                "total_fiber", "PAD680", "total_activity_min", "RIDAGEYR", "Female")
cat(sprintf("Complete cases for multivariate models: %d / %d\n",
            sum(complete.cases(data[multi_vars])), nrow(data)))
```

```{r}
# Survey Design — accounts for NHANES complex sampling
nhanes_design <- svydesign(
  id = ~SDMVPSU,
  strata = ~SDMVSTRA,
  weights = ~WTMEC2YR,
  data = data,
  nest = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
# Survey-Weighted OLS — Main Effects
# BMI: Fiber still strongest (p<0.001), sedentary time still sig (p=0.01), total_activity_min not sig (p=0.23).
#   More fiber = lower BMI. More sedentary time = higher BMI. Calories, sugar, protein not significant.
# Cholesterol: total_activity_min borderline (p=0.07), age and gender still primary.
# Glucose: total_activity_min IS significant (p=0.003) — more activity = lower glucose. New finding!

svy_bmi <- svyglm(
  BMXBMI ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_fiber + total_protein +
    PAD680 + total_activity_min + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)

summary(svy_bmi)

# Survey-Weighted OLS for Blood Cholesterol
svy_chol <- svyglm(
  LBXTC ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_fiber + total_protein +
    PAD680 + total_activity_min + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)

summary(svy_chol)

# Survey-Weighted OLS for Blood Glucose
svy_glucose_ols <- svyglm(
  LBDGLUSI ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_fiber + total_protein +
    PAD680 + total_activity_min + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)

summary(svy_glucose_ols)
```

```{r}
# VIF — All values under 5 (calories highest at 4.85), activity VIF only 1.01. No multicollinearity issues.

lm_for_vif <- lm(
  BMXBMI ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_fiber + total_protein +
    PAD680 + total_activity_min + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  data = data
)

cat("=== Variance Inflation Factors ===\n")
vif(lm_for_vif)
```

```{r}
# Regression Diagnostics — Q-Q shows slight tail departures but no major violations.
# No high-leverage outliers driving results. Residuals look reasonable.

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(lm_for_vif, main = "BMI Model Diagnostics")
```

```{r}
# Fiber x Activity(leisure) Interaction
# BMI: Interaction not significant (p=0.78). Fiber's BMI-lowering effect doesn't depend on activity.
# Cholesterol: Interaction not significant (p=0.36). Same story.
# ANOVA nested model tests confirm: adding the interaction doesn't improve fit for either outcome.
svy_int_bmi <- svyglm(
  BMXBMI ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_protein +
    Fiber_c + PAD680_c + Activity_c + Fiber_c:PAD680_c +
    RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)

summary(svy_int_bmi)

# Interaction model for Blood Cholesterol
svy_int_chol <- svyglm(
  LBXTC ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_protein +
    Fiber_c + PAD680_c + Activity_c + Fiber_c:PAD680_c +
    RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)

summary(svy_int_chol)

# Test whether the interaction term is significant (compare nested models)
svy_int_bmi_base <- svyglm(
  BMXBMI ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_protein +
    Fiber_c + PAD680_c + Activity_c + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)

cat("=== Interaction Test for BMI ===\n")
anova(svy_int_bmi_base, svy_int_bmi)

svy_int_chol_base <- svyglm(
  LBXTC ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_protein +
    Fiber_c + PAD680_c + Activity_c + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)

cat("=== Interaction Test for Cholesterol ===\n")
anova(svy_int_chol_base, svy_int_chol)
```

```{r}
# Multivariate Analysis — separate svyglm models per outcome (no survey-weighted MANOVA in R).
# Waist: Fiber (p=0.002) and sedentary time (p=0.004) still sig, activity not sig (p=0.20).
# Fiber x Activity(leisure) interaction for waist: borderline (p=0.07).
# Glucose: Only age (p<0.001) and gender (p<0.001) significant. No diet/activity effects.
# Joint tests: Fiber significant for BMI + waist, not cholesterol/glucose.
#              Activity significant for BMI + waist, not cholesterol/glucose.
#              Fiber x Activity interaction not significant for any outcome.
svy_waist <- svyglm(
  BMXWAIST ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_protein +
    Fiber_c + PAD680_c + Activity_c + Fiber_c:PAD680_c +
    RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)

svy_glucose <- svyglm(
  LBDGLUSI ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_protein +
    Fiber_c + PAD680_c + Activity_c + Fiber_c:PAD680_c +
    RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)

cat("=== Survey-Weighted Results: Waist Circumference ===\n")
summary(svy_waist)

cat("\n=== Survey-Weighted Results: Glucose ===\n")
summary(svy_glucose)

# Joint significance tests for key predictors across all 4 outcome models
cat("\n=== Joint Significance of Fiber (across all outcome models) ===\n")
regTermTest(svy_int_bmi, "Fiber_c")
regTermTest(svy_int_chol, "Fiber_c")
regTermTest(svy_waist, "Fiber_c")
regTermTest(svy_glucose, "Fiber_c")

cat("\n=== Joint Significance of Activity (across all outcome models) ===\n")
regTermTest(svy_int_bmi, "PAD680_c")
regTermTest(svy_int_chol, "PAD680_c")
regTermTest(svy_waist, "PAD680_c")
regTermTest(svy_glucose, "PAD680_c")

cat("\n=== Joint Significance of Fiber x Activity Interaction ===\n")
regTermTest(svy_int_bmi, "Fiber_c:PAD680_c")
regTermTest(svy_int_chol, "Fiber_c:PAD680_c")
regTermTest(svy_waist, "Fiber_c:PAD680_c")
regTermTest(svy_glucose, "Fiber_c:PAD680_c")
```

```{r}
# === BODY COMPOSITION ANALYSIS ===
# BMI alone can't separate fat from muscle. Waist circumference measures abdominal fat specifically.
# Waist-to-BMI ratio: higher = more fat relative to size, lower = more lean mass.
data$waist_bmi_ratio <- data$BMXWAIST / data$BMXBMI

# Update survey design with new variable
nhanes_design <- svydesign(
  id = ~SDMVPSU, strata = ~SDMVSTRA, weights = ~WTMEC2YR,
  data = data, nest = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
# Waist-to-BMI Ratio: Main Effects
# Protein still significant (p=0.006, negative) — more protein = lower ratio = more lean mass. Activity not sig.
# Fiber significant (p=0.001, positive) — more fiber = higher ratio = less mass overall (leaner people weigh less).
# Age (p<0.001) and Female (p<0.001) also significant — older and male = higher ratio.

svy_ratio_main <- svyglm(
  waist_bmi_ratio ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_fiber + total_protein +
    PAD680 + total_activity_min + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)
summary(svy_ratio_main)
```

```{r}
# Waist-to-BMI Ratio: Protein x Activity — not significant (p=0.66).
# Protein's lean-mass benefit is the same regardless of sedentary behavior.

svy_ratio_prot_act <- svyglm(
  waist_bmi_ratio ~ total_calories + total_sugar + Fiber_c + Protein_c +
    PAD680_c + Activity_c + Protein_c:PAD680_c + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)
summary(svy_ratio_prot_act)
```

```{r}
# Waist-to-BMI Ratio: Protein x Gender — not significant (p=0.12).
# Protein's lean-mass effect is similar for males and females.

svy_ratio_prot_gender <- svyglm(
  waist_bmi_ratio ~ total_calories + total_sugar + Fiber_c + Protein_c +
    PAD680_c + Activity_c + Protein_c:Female + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)
summary(svy_ratio_prot_gender)
```

```{r}
# Waist as Primary Outcome: Main Effects — protein NOT significant (p=0.59).
# Protein does not add belly fat. Fiber (p=0.001) and sedentary time (p=0.002) still significant.
# Key: protein is invisible here because it only affects lean mass, not abdominal fat.

svy_waist_main <- svyglm(
  BMXWAIST ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_fiber + total_protein +
    PAD680 + total_activity_min + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)
summary(svy_waist_main)
```

```{r}

    PAD680_c + Activity_c + Protein_c:PAD680_c + RIDAGEYR + Female,

summary(svy_waist_prot_act)
```


```{r}
# BMI Controlling for Waist — this isolates lean mass by holding abdominal fat constant.
# PROTEIN BECOMES SIGNIFICANT (p=0.009). At the same waist size, more protein = higher BMI.
# KEY FINDING: protein builds lean mass, not fat. BMI alone hid this because muscle and fat both raise BMI.

svy_bmi_adj_waist <- svyglm(
  BMXBMI ~ BMXWAIST + total_calories + total_sugar + total_fiber + total_protein +
    PAD680 + total_activity_min + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)
summary(svy_bmi_adj_waist)
```

```{r}
# BMI|Waist: Protein x Activity — borderline (p=0.07). Suggestive trend but not conclusive.

svy_bmi_adj_prot_act <- svyglm(
  BMXBMI ~ BMXWAIST + total_calories + total_sugar + Fiber_c + Protein_c +
    PAD680_c + Activity_c + Protein_c:PAD680_c + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)
summary(svy_bmi_adj_prot_act)
```

```{r}
# BMI|Waist: Protein x Gender — not significant (p=0.15). Lean-mass effect similar across sexes.

svy_bmi_adj_prot_gender <- svyglm(
  BMXBMI ~ BMXWAIST + total_calories + total_sugar + Fiber_c + Protein_c +
    PAD680_c + Activity_c + Protein_c:Female + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)
summary(svy_bmi_adj_prot_gender)
```

```{r}
# === PROTEIN SUMMARY TABLE ===
# BMI alone: p=0.10 (not sig) — protein hidden by fat/muscle confusion.
# Waist alone: p=0.59 (not sig) — protein doesn't add belly fat.
# BMI|Waist: p=0.009 (sig) — protein adds lean mass when fat is held constant.
# Waist/BMI ratio: p=0.004 (sig) — more protein = more lean mass relative to body size.
# CONCLUSION: BMI is a misleading outcome for protein. Use body composition measures instead.

svy_bmi_plain <- svyglm(
  BMXBMI ~ total_calories + total_sugar + total_fiber + total_protein +
    PAD680 + total_activity_min + RIDAGEYR + Female,
  design = nhanes_design
)

cat("=== Protein Effect Comparison ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Protein -> BMI (no control):         coef=%.5f, p=%.4f\n",
    coef(svy_bmi_plain)["total_protein"],
    summary(svy_bmi_plain)$coefficients["total_protein",4]))
cat(sprintf("Protein -> Waist:                    coef=%.5f, p=%.4f\n",
    coef(svy_waist_main)["total_protein"],
    summary(svy_waist_main)$coefficients["total_protein",4]))
cat(sprintf("Protein -> BMI (controlling waist):  coef=%.5f, p=%.4f\n",
    coef(svy_bmi_adj_waist)["total_protein"],
    summary(svy_bmi_adj_waist)$coefficients["total_protein",4]))
cat(sprintf("Protein -> Waist-to-BMI ratio:       coef=%.5f, p=%.4f\n",
    coef(svy_ratio_main)["total_protein"],
    summary(svy_ratio_main)$coefficients["total_protein",4]))
```
